rewrites.title: Inducible tethering of AP-1 at a silent reporter locus
rewrites.description: Tether a dimerized FOS-JUN (or bZIP fusion) to a transgenic silent reporter locus using dCas9 or a synthetic zinc-finger system under a doxycycline switch. After the tether is removed, measure whether accessibility and transcription persist, which tests whether AP-1 occupancy alone is sufficient to carry a self-sustaining memory state.

rewrites.title: Mitotic inheritance assay for AP-1-dependent memory
rewrites.description: Combine a stable (long-lived) fluorescent reporter of prior AP-1 activity with lineage tracking through several cell divisions, sorting and re-challenging daughter cells by their inherited reporter state. If primed responsiveness is inherited by daughters at rates above chance and tracks reporter dilution, memory is transmitted through mitosis; if it is lost, the memory must be re-established after each division.

rewrites.title: Persistence and heritability timescales of an endogenous AP-1 reporter
rewrites.description: Track an endogenous AP-1 reporter, such as a knock-in FOS-HaloTag or an AP-1 motif-driven fluorophore, by live imaging across many divisions. Extract state autocorrelation times, mother-daughter correlations, and switching rates to distinguish true multigenerational memory from slow protein turnover.

rewrites.title: Heterokaryon fusion and nuclear/cytoplasmic swap
rewrites.description: Fuse primed to naive cells (and primed nuclei to naive cytoplasts via enucleation or nuclear transfer) with allele-distinguishable reporters, then score allele-specific AP-1 target induction in the hybrid. Dominance of the primed state and whether it is nucleus- or cytoplasm-borne identifies the physical substrate, and recruitment of the naive genome would indicate a diffusible trans-acting AP-1 memory rather than a cis-chromatin one.

rewrites.title: Degron depletion of FOS/JUN after priming
rewrites.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) before re-stimulation. If enhanced response and accessibility persist without AP-1, memory is held elsewhere. If they collapse, AP-1 is required for maintenance.

rewrites.title: Mutual information between stimulus history and AP-1 state after washout
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined library of past stimulus histories, then after a long washout quantify, cell by cell, the mutual information between which history a cell experienced and its current AP-1 occupancy, AP-1 motif accessibility, and target transcript counts. This yields the number of bits of past experience retained, a decay-rate curve for that information over time and divisions, and a direct test of how much of the retained information is lost when AP-1 components are degraded during the washout.

rewrites.title: Pulse-train response and transfer-function fitting of AP-1 dynamics
rewrites.description: Use optogenetic ERK/RAS control or microfluidics to deliver pulse trains that vary in frequency, duration, and spacing. Then fit linear and nonlinear transfer-function models to AP-1 reporter dynamics and downstream enhancer opening. If the fitted decay time constant is much longer than the turnover of AP-1 protein and mRNA, the memory sits downstream of AP-1 (e.g., in chromatin), not in AP-1 levels themselves.

rewrites.title: Multi-week in vivo cofactor dependence screen
rewrites.description: After a defined inflammatory or stress challenge in mice, use conditional knockouts or inhibitors of cofactors such as p300, BRD4, or SWI/SNF components at different times to see which ones must stay active for AP-1-driven chromatin changes to persist. Tissue-level CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq over weeks would show whether the memory is maintained by a cofactor-dependent chromatin state.

rewrites.title: Lineage tracing across divisions with sibling-pair and mitotic-bookmarking assays
rewrites.description: Label cells with a heritable barcode or Cre-based memory reporter at the time of AP-1 activation and follow their daughters for many divisions. Use sibling-pair and mitotic-bookmarking assays (live imaging plus mitotic-chromosome ChIP) to determine whether AP-1 binding or its downstream chromatin marks (H3K27ac, accessibility) are inherited and correlate with persistent expression.

rewrites.title: Priming learning curve with a decay term
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells a controlled number of times with systematically varied rest intervals and fit the re-challenge response to a Wright-type learning curve in which cumulative exposures are discounted by a decay factor, yielding a per-gene and per-enhancer AP-1 memory half-life. Adding an unrelated second stimulus measures transfer of the primed response, separating stimulus-specific memory from a general increase in responsiveness.

rewrites.title: Re-stimulation kinetics as the functional readout
rewrites.description: Prime cells, allow the primary response to resolve, then re-stimulate and measure response latency, amplitude, and responding-cell fraction by live imaging or time-resolved sequencing. Memory predicts faster or larger secondary induction specifically at AP-1-bound loci, which should vanish when AP-1 sites are mutated.

rewrites.title: Control loci and control stimuli for specificity
rewrites.description: Compare AP-1 motif-containing loci that were never bound with those that were, and compare cells given an unrelated stimulus (e.g., a different signaling pathway) with AP-1-stimulated cells. Add motif-mutation or CRISPR-edited enhancer controls so that any retained accessibility or priming is shown to be specific to prior AP-1 binding and not to general stress or cell-state changes.

rewrites.title: Phospho-degron stabilized versus wild-type FOS and JUN
rewrites.description: Generate matched FOS or JUN variants with altered phospho-degron or ubiquitin-site mutations that change protein half-life while keeping transcriptional output comparable, using pulse-chase protein measurements. If longer-lived AP-1 protein extends chromatin memory independently of transcript levels, protein persistence itself would be the memory substrate, as with stabilized ΔFosB.

rewrites.title: Mutual information between past stimulus history and current single-cell state
rewrites.description: Expose cells to defined stimulus histories, remove the stimulus, and wait varying times. Then calculate the mutual information between the past history and the present single-cell state (scATAC/scRNA) at AP-1 targets versus non-AP-1 loci. Test whether AP-1 inhibition lowers the number of bits retained or makes the information fade faster.

rewrites.title: Re-stimulation kinetics and priming assays
rewrites.description: Compare the transcriptional and AP-1 binding response to a second identical stimulus in naive versus previously stimulated cells, measuring the speed, amplitude, and gene set of the response (e.g., by time-resolved RNA-seq or live single-cell reporters). Faster or stronger re-induction of the same target genes in primed cells, and dependence of that priming on the original AP-1 pulse, would support a memory function rather than a simple dose response.

rewrites.title: Frequency-dependent probing of the AP-1 response
rewrites.description: Drive AP-1 with small periodic pulses across a range of frequencies in naive versus previously stimulated cells, and measure the amplitude and phase lag of a live-cell reporter (e.g., a FRET or luciferase AP-1 sensor). A history-dependent change in the slow relaxation component, absent in naive cells, would indicate an internal memory state that the fast pulses cannot erase.

rewrites.title: Priming-history matrix with mutual information
rewrites.description: Systematically vary priming dose, pulse duration, pulse frequency, and interval, and measure re-stimulation response at multiple decay timepoints. Compute the mutual information between priming history and the response to determine how much information the AP-1 system stores and for how long. This tests the single-stimulus, single-timescale, and fixed-definition assumptions.

rewrites.title: Targeted epigenome editing and sufficiency tests at AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Use dCas9 tools (e.g., dCas9-FOS or dCas9-KRAB) or motif mutation at specific AP-1-dependent enhancers. Test whether opening or closing them alters the response to a later challenge, and whether forcing AP-1 binding in naive cells can mimic memory. Combine this with histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) and pioneer-factor partner tests (e.g., with BAF/SWI-SNF) to identify mechanism.

rewrites.title: Allele-specific memory with motif-variant genetics
rewrites.description: Use cells from hybrid or heterozygous individuals and allele-specific ATAC and RNA after priming to compare alleles differing in AP-1 motif strength (natural variants or base-edited alleles). Dose-dependent, cis-restricted persistence of accessibility and enhanced re-induction would show that memory is encoded locally at AP-1 sites, not in trans through diffusible signals.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis test for bistable AP-1 feedback
rewrites.description: Titrate an AP-1-activating input up from zero and down from saturation, measuring steady-state AP-1 reporter output at matched doses along each arm. Non-overlapping up and down curves at the same dose would demonstrate hysteresis, indicating a self-sustaining feedback memory rather than a passive stimulus-tracking response.
